reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Snake Who Paid Cash with its ending on The Unsocial Swans page; the frame (Red-Eye to King Foe-Crusher) is stated and omitted, and the inner tale is dropped with disclosure.
The farmer's caste is dropped and disclosed; the snake is a 'guardian' only in the farmer's own words, never divine in the narration.

Age band 12+: the boy's death is two calm sentences, never drawn. The father's 'death that suited his intelligence' is framed as a greedy bid for the snake's trust and answered by the snake; the story blames greed, not the dead boy.
No em dashes; the pause question comes before the blow.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; one Codex gpt-5.6-sol generation with seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text.
The blow, the bite, the boy's death and the pyre are not drawn; panel 4 shows only the stick hidden behind the boy's back.
The mourning panel shows two relatives comforting the farmer with no pyre, smoke or body; the cobra is a natural snake with no divine marks or human features.
No caste markers or modern objects; similar natural skin tones. Three alt texts were corrected after review to match the pictures.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; edited panels were re-checked by a separate agent.
